artworks.title: Jupiter and Semele
artworks.description: Moreau's Jupiter and Semele — the mortal mother consumed by the god's true form, Dionysus still unborn in the blaze.

artworks.title: The Death of Semele
artworks.description: Rubens' Death of Semele — Hera's jealous counsel fulfilled as the thunderbolt that births Bacchus kills his mother.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Semele
artworks.description: Tintoretto's Jupiter and Semele — Venetian drama of the visitation that seals Thebes' wine-god lineage.

artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.description: Caravaggio's Bacchus — the god who survives the fire, twice-born from Zeus' thigh after Semele's death.

popCulture.title: Semele
popCulture.description: The Theban princess who asks to see Zeus unveiled — and dies so Dionysus can be born from the god's thigh.

popCulture.title: Dionysus
popCulture.description: Twice-born from fire and thigh — Semele's death is the wine-god's first myth of arrival.
